title: The Drowned Oath
premise: Cyrus Almeida, last sworn smuggler of the Almeida guild, takes in a mute child who speaks the drowned tongue of Thornfell's buried court and discovers the girl is a soul-price: a payment owed on an oath her grandfather sold generations ago to keep the guild alive. To free her, Cyrus must retrace every road her family ever built—through flooded mines, forgotten shrines, and the court beneath the mountain—while the guild's creditors and the mountain's ancient debtors close in from both sides. In the end Cyrus learns the oath can only be broken by someone willing to take its place, and she pays it herself, trading her freedom below for the child's life above, leaving the guild reborn under the girl's care.
about_author: Y. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping cave systems across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about debts, borders, and the people who carry both.

chapters.title: Salt on the Lintel
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. The last active smuggler of a dying guild runs one final cargo through Thornfell and returns to find the guildhall cold, her uncle dead, and the ledgers burned. Beat: grief sharpened into stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. A barefoot girl appears during a storm, speaking a language no living kingdom uses—and the wards over the door answer her. Beat: unease blooming into recognition that something old has found them.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Didn't Burn
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV, with fragments of her grandfather's hidden journal. She finds a page recording a 'soul-price, paid in full, owed in kind' dated the year the guild was founded. Beat: dread of inheritance.

chapters.title: The Tongue Beneath Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and the child (rendered as impressionistic dream-POV). The girl's words map onto the oldest tunnels Cyrus knows; the language names places that have no modern names. Beat: wonder laced with fear.

chapters.title: Creditors at the Gate
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. A rival syndicate arrives claiming the guild's debts, including one marked 'non-negotiable, held below.' They want the child. Beat: the world closes in.

chapters.title: Nine Roads Out
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. She flees with the girl through smugglers' paths, testing which routes are watched. A near-capture forces her first kill in years. Beat: survival's cost made visceral.

chapters.title: The Shrine That Drinks
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a drowned shrine, the girl speaks clearly for the first time: 'You owe me.' The water rises around them without touching her. Beat: revelation—the child is not random; she is collateral.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Oath
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV via journal interludes. She pieces together how the guild bought its fortune by selling a future member's soul to the court beneath the mountain. Beat: fury at the dead who signed her name before she existed.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Hounds
chapters.summary: Syndicate enforcer Vess POV. Vess tracks them, motivated by her own debt-bond to the syndicate—a mirror of Cyrus's inherited oath. Beat: antagonist humanized.

chapters.title: Flooded Mine, Burning Lantern
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. An escape through a collapsing mine nearly drowns them both; the girl calms the water. Cyrus realizes the child's power grows as they near the mountain. Beat: reluctant awe.

chapters.title: A Name in the Drowned Tongue
chapters.summary: The girl POV (fragmentary). She remembers being someone else once, long ago, and being promised back. Beat: identity horror—the child may be older than the guild.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. A river smuggler demands payment in memories; Cyrus trades her memory of her mother's face. Beat: the price-of-survival theme made literal and intimate.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: First glimpse POV. Deep below, the ancient court stirs, aware its collateral walks toward it. Introduce the Oathkeeper, its patient herald. Beat: menace from below begins.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. She bargains with a disgraced guild archivist, Odile, who knows the oath's legal structure: souls can be reclaimed if a greater price is offered. Beat: hope with fine print.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Closes
chapters.summary: Vess POV. Vess corners them at a border shrine but hesitates when the girl speaks Vess's own bond-debt aloud. Beat: enemy wavering.

chapters.title: What Survives Is What You Carry
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV, quiet chapter. Camped in high passes, she teaches the girl stars and roads; the girl teaches her three words of the drowned tongue. Beat: love forming where duty began.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile POV. The archive reveals other guilds made similar oaths—all their children taken. The court has been fed for centuries. Beat: scale of horror widens.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Salt Cellars
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Odile sells their location to buy her own archive's safety. Capture; separation. Beat: trust broken, lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: The Cage of Brass and Law
chapters.summary: The girl POV. Held by the syndicate, she hears the court speaking through the stone, counting down her delivery date. Beat: ticking clock made explicit—seven days.

chapters.title: Negotiation with Wolves
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Brought before the syndicate's master, she offers the guild's remaining fortune for the girl and is refused: only the court can release a claimed soul. Beat: money cannot solve this.

chapters.title: Vess Turns
chapters.summary: Vess POV. Haunted by the girl naming her bond, Vess frees them in the night, paying with her own standing. Beat: redemption seeded at cost.

chapters.title: Descent Begins
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. They enter the mountain through the First Road, sealed since the guild's founding. The dark answers the girl's voice. Beat: threshold crossed, no return.

chapters.title: Roads My Family Built
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Traps and tests left by her ancestors guard the way—built to keep the court's things in, or perhaps to keep oath-breakers out. Beat: legacy as labyrinth.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In an underwater chapel they find the original contract, written in blood and salt, bearing her grandfather's signature—and a blank line awaiting hers. Beat: the trap of inheritance revealed.

chapters.title: The Oathkeeper Speaks
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. The court's herald offers terms: the girl stays, or a volunteer of equal blood takes her place. It has waited two hundred years; it can wait longer. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Seven Days, Six Left
chapters.summary: The girl POV. She tells Cyrus to leave—that she was always meant for this—but her hands shake. Beat: sacrifice refused, compassion deepened.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile POV. Guilt-ridden, she arrives uninvited with the one loophole: an oath sworn under false pretenses can be voided if the original lie is proven before the court. Beat: fragile plan formed.

chapters.title: The Lie at the Guild's Root
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Digging through ancestral testimony, she finds it: the first Almeida never owned what he sold—he sold the court a soul that belonged to the mountain itself. Beat: the whole economy of the oath is fraud.

chapters.title: The Syndicate Descends
chapters.summary: Villain POV. The syndicate, tipped off, floods into the lower roads to seize the girl and claim the court's favor for themselves. Beat: all factions converge.

chapters.title: Battle in the Bone Galleries
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, kinetic. Running fight through ossuary tunnels; Vess falls holding the line so Cyrus and the girl can reach the court. Beat: sacrifice, grief mid-motion.

chapters.title: Audience with the Drowned Court
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Before the throne of the old king beneath the mountain, she presents evidence of the fraudulent sale. The court listens—it, too, was cheated. Beat: climax's fulcrum.

chapters.title: Verdict of Salt
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. The court voids the oath but demands restitution: the stolen years must be returned by someone. The blank line in the contract glows. Beat: victory curdling into choice.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV, interior. She understands at last: survival was never free; someone always paid. She signs—not to replace the girl, but to repay the mountain what was taken from it. Beat: thematic resolution embraced.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The girl walks free into daylight as Cyrus descends; the mountain seals behind her with something like gratitude. Beat: heartbreak rendered as symmetry.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Open Door
chapters.summary: The girl POV. Above ground, she grieves, then finds Cyrus's journal left to her, every road mapped, every toll noted. Beat: inheritance transformed into gift.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Guild
chapters.summary: The girl POV, years later framing begins. With Odile and freed survivors of other oaths, she refounds the guild—not to smuggle goods, but to smuggle souls home. Beat: purpose born of loss.

chapters.title: Letters Down the Mountain
chapters.summary: Epistolary chapter. The girl writes letters she leaves at the sealed gate; once, impossibly, a reply comes in Cyrus's hand: 'Keep the roads open.' Beat: hope against reason.

chapters.title: The Court Remembers Kindness
chapters.summary: The girl POV. The mountain, repaid, loosens its grip: it grants the new guild passage rights and hints a debt honestly held can be worked off. Beat: the system can change.

chapters.title: Descent of Her Own
chapters.summary: The girl POV. Now grown, she leads her first rescue into the deep, following Cyrus's maps, and finds the first marker of a road back up. Beat: agency fully assumed.

chapters.title: The Drowned Oath, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Final dual POV. At the gate, the girl speaks the old tongue and the new: the oath is rewritten so no child is ever again born into debt. Far below, a lantern moves along a road that wasn't there before. Beat: closure, continuity, quiet triumph.
